notes.sowing: Sow directly from 1 to 2 weeks before your last frost, {cm:0.6} deep in rows {cm:30} apart, and thin to about {cm:20}. Dill has a taproot and dislikes transplanting. Sow again every 3 weeks for a steady supply of leaves, and in late summer for fall.
notes.care: Grow in full sun in a sheltered spot, as tall plants can blow over. Water in dry spells to delay flowering. Leave the striped swallowtail caterpillars that feed on it; the flowers also draw hoverflies, lacewings and small wasps.
notes.harvest: Pick leaves from about 6 weeks after sowing. For seed, cut heads 2 to 3 weeks after flowering, once the seeds turn brown, and dry them in a paper bag. Plants left to seed will sow themselves.
